activity.title: Proud of you!

Something has shifted in the air recently. These days, the AgentMail crew: - ships a lot - sleeps too little The customers have gotten a lot bigger. The team remains small. When I wasn't building, I always thought about what the opportunity cost of not doing it looked like. What was the next thing I could be doing? What did I actually want to do with my life? Now that you feel like you're doing what you want, you start to think about the opportunity cost of doing it. Especially when it gets hard. You see the work-life balance and the vacations and PTO.... man that seems pretty nice. But I started realizing the way out is always going to be there. No matter what you do. There's always another thing you wanna do. Man, that would be nice. But if you get a rare chance to do what feels like your life's work, why not be delusionally optimistic? Why not love the late nights and the hard weeks and everything else that comes with it? Why not give everything and all to it? There's always going to be a shiny new thing to chase. But I heard once that you don't realize the good days until you've left them. And man, do I feel good about what we're building :)

Celebrating Our GitHub Interns As Cohort A wraps up their 12-week internship journey, we're taking a moment to celebrate and thank this incredible group of interns for the impact they've made across GitHub. Over the past three months, our interns have contributed to meaningful work across Engineering, Product, Revenue and Communications. From shipping features and improving processes to tackling complex challenges and bringing fresh perspectives, they've made valuable contributions that will continue to have a lasting impact on our teams and products. The photo below was taken during Intern Week (July 13-17) at our San Francisco headquarters, where a group of interns from our Engineering and Product teams came together in person. While not every intern was able to join onsite, today we celebrate all of our interns, wherever they worked from. Cohort A: Thank you for the curiosity, creativity, dedication, and energy you've brought to GitHub. It has been inspiring to watch your growth, and we're excited to see what comes next in your journey. Congratulations on completing your internship, and thank you for being part of GitHub. #GitHubInterns #LifeAtGitHub #FutureTalent #InternshipExperience Photo: Intern Week at GitHub HQ in San Francisco (July 13-17, 2026) featuring Engineering and Product interns.

We launched AgentMail (YC S25) on Y Combinator one year ago today. For any founder reading this, the biggest thing we learned: Launch early and often - don’t stake all your bet on one launch going perfect. We put so much time and effort into this one, but a 40 second hiring agent demo with 2010s NCR dubstep music overperformed it! Momentum matters and compounds - keep shipping and keep shouting. People will listen eventually :)
AgentMail is now an official plugin on OpenAI. For all you Codex users, this one is for you!

I am happy to share that I am starting a new position at DeepAware AI (YC S25) ! Backed by Y Combinator and NVIDIA , DeepAware is building full-stack Physical AI, with one of the largest robotics fleets in the US including humanoids and quadrupeds. I will be working on developing and integrating autonomous systems across the fleet and at customer deployment sites. Thank you to all my colleagues at VALT Health , proud of what we built together. Excited to be a part of the future of physical AI!

What if AI could help accelerate the search for tomorrow's medicines? 🧬 This summer, OLCF intern Dhruva Bhat ( University of California, Berkeley ) worked with his mentor, Debsindhu Bhowmik on their project, "An Evidence-Guided Generative AI Pipeline for Enzyme-Specific Substrate and Mutation Design." They developed a traceable AI workflow that combines target-specific biological evidence with tournament-based AI reasoning and diffusion models to generate potential enzyme substrates and mutations. By grounding AI-generated results in biological evidence, the project helps improve confidence in the design process while creating a transparent path from data to discovery. 🔗 Learn more about internship opportunities at Oak Ridge National Laboratory : https://lnkd.in/gjBgiigR #DrugDiscovery #ComputationalBiology #BigScience

Super excited to have had the opportunity to compete in the Astera Labs Intern Hackathon! Through much deliberation and design my incredible team of 7 was able to create a software which catches miscommunications and false specification before communications are released to the public. For this idea and our presentation we were selected by COO Sanjay Gajendra out of more than 130 interns to have our idea funded and made a reality! A huge shout-out to my teammates Aditi J. , Angelina Haroutyunian , Claire Lee , Harsh Shah , Neha N. , and Sahil Handa as well as our mentors Jenna Ellis and Pranav N. as we would have never gotten this far without working as well together as we did.
